source_snapshot.test_set: Intel GNR CPU RAS - Memory Demand and Patrol Scrub
source_snapshot.procedure: Configure the Intel CScripts/ELog/WHEA/error-injection/firmware-first matrix and DDR5 ECS; preserve/clear the selected MC and retry valid state; halt and inject a CE at 0x10000 with `immConsume=False`; consume it explicitly with `mem(0x10000)`; inspect mc0/ch0 machine-check and retry entry; resume and check serial handling.

source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. Demand Scrub specific BIOS setup : EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration > — DDR5 ECS = Enable 2.Ensure the machine check status register and retry_rd_err_log valid bits are cleared. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.showsearch("mc_status_shadow") >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mcs.chs.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log.v >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log[1].show() 3. Inject a correctable error. >>> halt() >>> ei.utils.resetInjectorLockCheck() >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(0x10000, errType="ce", immConsume=False) 4. Consume the error by reading the memory address. >>> mem(0x10000) 5. Check the machine check bank registers and check a memory read error was detected. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.showsearch("mc_status_shadow") >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc_status_shadow.show() 6. Check the retry_rd_err_logs that the error was logged. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log[1].show() 7. Resume the system and check the serial log that BIOS handled the error. >>> go() 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

test_case.test_name: Demand Scrub — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Demonstrate that a correctable memory error planted without immediate consumption is consumed by a demand read on the intended Intel GNR DIMM and reported through the expected firmware-first machine-check, retry-read and FTrace ELog path.
required_package: GNR CPU stepping, BIOS/BMC/OS, DIMM PN/serial/slot and socket/IMC/channel topology
Intel CScripts/error-injection package version/hash/license and exact `immConsume=False`/`mem()` semantics
Project mapping/restoration for every source BIOS/DFX/ELog/WHEA/firmware-first/GRUB knob
Address0x10000 to physical target mapping and mc0.ch0 retry_rd_err_log[1] ownership
Expected clean prestate, correctable MC shadow/MSCOD, retry entry and FTrace extlog_mem_event fields/timing
Dedicated window, serial/OOB path, halt/read/go timeouts, wrong-severity/crash recovery and no-retry plan
test_case.test_command: Record immutable platform and DIMM topology, harness version and BIOS/GRUB baseline; apply/verify the exact source enablement matrix and DDR5 ECS; map address0x10000 plus mc0/ch0/retry index1 to the intended DIMM; preserve evidence and establish the approved clean register prestate; halt, reset injector lock and issue one CE with `immConsume=False`; capture proof that injection did not already consume; execute `mem(0x10000)` once; capture the named MC shadow and retry entry, resume, collect serial/FTrace extlog/OS/SEL evidence, verify health and restore settings under the recovery plan.
test_case.expected_result: Check the FTrace logs to ensure that an ELog record was logged indicated by extlog_mem_event.

safety_gate: Use a dedicated workload-free SUT with stable power, serial and independent OOB recovery
Preserve general dmesg/journal/SEL/FTrace evidence and BIOS/GRUB baseline; do not perform blanket log clearing
Clear only approved target MC/retry state after capture, and prove the correct target/index
Do not assume 0x10000 is a safe or intended memory location; require vendor harness mapping
Verify the error remains latent after injection and stop if it is consumed early or appears on the wrong channel
Stop on fatal/uncorrectable severity, unexpected MCA, hang, crash or missing response; never automatically reinject or reboot
After evidence capture restore all lock/DFX/error-injection/GRUB settings and verify memory/OS/BMC health
expected_evidence: Harness version/hash and before/after BIOS/GRUB configuration matrix
Preserved baseline plus clean selected mc_status_shadow and retry index1 evidence
One exact injection transcript showing CE `immConsume=False` and no premature consumption
Explicit `mem(0x10000)` result followed by expected correctable MC shadow and retry log
Serial handling, timestamped FTrace `extlog_mem_event`, OS/SEL correlation, final health/restoration and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Reference BIOS paths may be remapped only with an explicit functional equivalence matrix. `ras=cec_disable` is optional source guidance and, if used, requires approved GRUB backup/rebuild/reboot/restoration.
